evidence.exact_quote: 1. **Conversational ledger mode** — normal chat while Jared specs a feature. Codex updates the ledger after every substantive turn. Goal Mode is optional and usually unnecessary here.

items.impact: Establishes the interactive operating mode and its mandatory per-turn persistence behavior.
items.statement: Conversational feature specification uses the ledger, requires updates after every substantive turn, and does not normally require Goal Mode.
items.title: Conversational ledger mode is the default interactive path

evidence.exact_quote: Do not treat “Generate node-readiness report” as permission to create WorkNodes.

items.impact: Prevents a reporting command from crossing into executable task creation.
items.statement: Node-readiness reporting grants no authority to create WorkNodes.
items.title: Readiness reporting has an explicit execution boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Each ledger directory must include manifest, events, records, state, validation, indexes, and source_shards directories.

items.impact: Defines the minimum persistent structure expected of each registered ledger.
items.statement: Every ledger has a required directory structure covering source, state, records, validation, and indexes.
items.title: Ledger storage shape is prescribed

evidence.exact_quote: Read full `events.jsonl`, `source_shards/**`, or legacy `working_ledger.md` only when a compact state file points to a specific source_ref that must be inspected.

items.impact: Bounds routine context loading while preserving an evidence-triggered path to detailed history.
items.statement: Detailed ledger history and shards may be read only when compact state identifies a specific required source reference.
items.title: Resume reads are deliberately minimized

evidence.exact_quote: 5. Update `state/current.json`, `state/handoff.json`, `state/open_items.json`, and `state/compile_queue.json`.

items.impact: A crash or concurrent writer can leave projections mutually inconsistent, and the workflow provides no detection, retry, rollback, or reconciliation oracle.
items.statement: The multi-file per-turn update contract does not define atomicity, idempotency, locking, write ordering, partial-write recovery, or a consistency check across the event and projection files.
items.title: Per-turn persistence lacks a transaction protocol

evidence.exact_quote: If an item mixes GUI and non-GUI work, split it when safe. If not safe, mark `gui_related=true` and preserve a split recommendation in notes.

items.impact: Different agents can classify or split the same mixed atom differently, and routing metadata alone does not guarantee that accessibility or localization obligations survive compilation.
items.statement: The rule does not define when splitting is safe, how to validate classification consistency, or how GUI accessibility and localization requirements are represented rather than merely labeled.
items.title: Mixed GUI classification leaves material discretion

evidence.exact_quote: 2. Refuse false completion if open blockers, unresolved high-level questions, unclassified candidates, or contradictions remain.

items.impact: The correct no-compile policy exists, but agents can disagree about whether a question is high-level or a contradiction remains.
items.statement: Compilation is barred by unresolved planning conditions, but the document supplies no deterministic query, severity threshold, or validator result that proves each condition absent.
items.title: Compilation refusal is correct but not fully falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: - coverage map for every original span;

items.statement: Standardization requires an explicit coverage disposition for every source span, alongside identity and reference preservation controls.
items.title: Plan standardization has a span-level losslessness oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - validators after each batch.

items.impact: A failing validator can reveal damage without defining whether the batch is reverted, repaired in place, quarantined, or resumed.
items.statement: Batch validation is required, but the standardization flow does not state rollback boundaries, checkpoint format, or restart behavior after a batch fails.
items.title: Standardization has detection but no failed-batch recovery contract

evidence.exact_quote: The node-readiness report may classify future readiness and blockers, including `gui_related` routing inheritance. It must not create WorkNodes or executable build tasks.

items.impact: Supports downstream readiness consumers without silently creating executable work.
items.statement: The generated readiness surface may report and propagate routing metadata but remains non-executable.
items.title: Index outputs are informative rather than executable

evidence.exact_quote: This workflow section consumes `PLS-012` and `PDS-014`; those owner PlanUnits define the durable registry, closed-world scope manifest, deterministic finding and check keys, repair impact matrix, repair closure matrix, and validator behavior.

items.impact: Names the owner PlanUnits and makes this workflow a consumer rather than a competing contract owner.
items.statement: Semantic-audit mechanics are owned by PLS-012 and PDS-014 and consumed by this workflow.
items.title: Audit closure has explicit cross-document ownership

evidence.exact_quote: Each row is keyed by a deterministic `finding_key` derived from `finding_family`, `ledger_id`, `source_atom_ids`, `plan_unit_ids`, `owner_docs`, `detail_keys`, and `exact_tokens`. The registry row preserves `closure_id`, `finding_key`, `finding_family`, `ledger_id`, `audit_ids`, `source_atom_ids`, `plan_unit_ids`, `owner_docs`, `consumer_docs`, `detail_keys`, `exact_tokens`, `closure_status`, `closure_evidence`, `closure_reason`, `hashes`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_by_audit_id`, and `reopen_conditions`.

items.impact: Allows equivalent findings to retain identity and closure history across audits.
items.statement: Closure rows use a content-derived finding key and retain lineage, evidence, status, timestamps, and reopen conditions.
items.title: Semantic closure identity is content-derived and durable

evidence.exact_quote: Each row is keyed by a deterministic `finding_key` derived from `finding_family`, `ledger_id`, `source_atom_ids`, `plan_unit_ids`, `owner_docs`, `detail_keys`, and `exact_tokens`.

items.impact: Untrusted or sensitive exact tokens can become durable key material, while simultaneous writers or unbounded rows can compromise privacy, uniqueness, performance, and supportability.
items.statement: The JSONL registry contract omits token normalization and size limits, sensitive-value handling, retention or deletion rules, access controls, collision handling, locking, compaction, and concurrent-append recovery.
items.title: Closure registry lifecycle and multi-writer behavior are unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: Before semantic review, the audit writes `audit_scope_manifest.jsonl` with deterministic `check_id` rows for compiled atom details, compile targets, added/changed PlanUnit claims, reciprocal `source_lineage`, owner/consumer routes, schema/contract identity, `depends_on`/`unblocks` edges, synchronized ledger projection fields, index/governance checks, and forbidden-artifact checks. Completion requires every scope row to be classified.

items.impact: Establishes a closed-world review inventory and a measurable completion condition across producers, consumers, dependencies, projections, and forbidden outputs.
items.statement: Every deterministic scope check must be classified before semantic review can complete.
items.title: Scope manifest is the audit completeness oracle

evidence.exact_quote: `BLOCKED` is used only when `repair_required=true`, a validator fails or mutates state, forbidden artifacts exist, or a user decision is required. `PASS_WITH_WARNINGS` is terminal when all findings have `repair_required=false`; `PASS` means no findings.

items.impact: Prevents non-actionable observations from falsely blocking while keeping failures, mutation, forbidden outputs, and user decisions blocking.
items.statement: Audit terminal states are determined by actionable findings and concrete blocking conditions, with PASS reserved for zero findings.
items.title: Audit outcome states have explicit predicates

evidence.exact_quote: Audits record `subject_ref` as the latest substantive commit touching live `Plans/**`, target-ledger governing state, `.plan_index`, governance artifacts, or process scripts.

items.impact: Different implementations can choose different baselines when multiple relevant histories or merge commits exist, undermining repeatable currentness decisions.
items.statement: The term latest substantive commit is not operationalized for merges, multiple roots, path renames, shallow history, or ties across the listed surfaces.
items.title: Subject reference selection is not fully deterministic

evidence.exact_quote: Ledger `latest_audit_*` fields point to the latest state-certifying audit or repair that changed or validated canonical Plans, ledger governing state, index, or governance. Audit-only observations and hygiene repairs do not stale or restamp ledger projections.

items.impact: Prevents audit-only churn from presenting itself as a new certification of governed state.
items.statement: Ledger audit pointers advance only for state-certifying work, not audit-only or hygiene-only activity.
items.title: Certification projection excludes observation-only churn

evidence.exact_quote: Deep audits read the registry before writing new risks. If a finding is already closed and the source atom, PlanUnit, owner evidence, and closure evidence hashes are unchanged, the audit records `previously_closed` with `repair_required=false` and does not emit the item as a new semantic warning.

items.impact: Suppresses duplicate risk while allowing hash-driven reopening when governed evidence changes.
items.statement: Unchanged closed findings remain non-actionable and are represented as previously closed instead of reissued.
items.title: Closure registry prevents duplicate semantic findings

evidence.exact_quote: Bounded repairs write `repair_impact_matrix.jsonl` before editing when the latest audit has at least one `repair_required=true` source row. The impact matrix maps every actionable finding to synchronized files, PlanUnits, schemas, dependency edges, owner refs, ledger projection fields, index artifacts, governance artifacts, and covered scope checks.

items.impact: Forces repair propagation to be inventoried across every governed consumer before canonical editing begins.
items.statement: Actionable repairs require a pre-edit impact map covering canonical owners, consumers, projections, indexes, governance, and scope checks.
items.title: Repair impact mapping precedes edits

evidence.exact_quote: If the latest audit has zero actionable rows, the repair must refuse/no-op and must not revalidate `previously_closed` rows or create registry rows for them.

items.impact: Eliminates repair churn and registry mutation when no actionable source row exists.
items.statement: A repair has no authority to proceed or restamp closure state when the latest audit has no actionable findings.
items.title: Zero-action repair is a mandatory no-op

evidence.exact_quote: Repair may finish only with `repair_required_count=0` or a true user decision; passing validators alone are insufficient.

items.impact: Blocks false completion based on syntax or structural validation while actionable semantic work remains.
items.statement: Post-repair completion requires semantic closure over the original and expanded impact scope, not merely passing validators.
items.title: Semantic closure, not validator success, controls repair completion

evidence.exact_quote: python3 scripts/pm-audit-closure.py validate --audit-dir Plans/.audits/<audit_id> --require-closure-matrix

items.impact: Operators cannot distinguish a semantic validation failure from environment, dependency, filesystem, or network-related execution failure using this workflow alone.
items.statement: The required validator command is concrete, but expected exit codes, diagnostics, artifact outputs, retry behavior, offline assumptions, and recovery from unavailable dependencies are not defined here.
items.title: Validator operational failure semantics are absent

evidence.exact_quote: Run only after docs and generated indexes are stable. Then regenerate governance artifacts, refresh Spec Lock, run plan/shard validators, and certify changed files/blockers/risks.

items.impact: An agent can seal while documents or indexes are still changing because stable has no defined observation interval, clean-state check, or hash-based predicate.
items.statement: Governance sealing is correctly ordered after stability, but the workflow does not provide a machine-checkable definition of stable or a failure/rollback path if regeneration or validators mutate or fail.
items.title: Governance seal precondition is not operationalized

evidence.exact_quote: Ledger-to-Plans compile phases that exceed atom, owner-doc, or document-size thresholds must use bounded read-only subagents with assignment/result evidence. The parent/controller remains the only canonical writer.

items.impact: The one-writer safety model is clear, but agents may invoke or omit sharding inconsistently and cannot prove that a large compile stayed within safe capacity.
items.statement: Large compiles require bounded read-only subagents and a sole canonical writer, but the atom, owner-document, document-size, concurrency, assignment, timeout, retry, and result-acceptance thresholds are not specified here.
items.title: Compile sharding has a clear authority model but undefined limits

evidence.exact_quote: Continue ledger <ledger_id>.

items.impact: Malformed, adversarial, localized, or ambiguous identifiers can be interpreted inconsistently or used to address unintended ledger paths.
items.statement: The supported phrase interface does not define parsing, escaping, normalization, authorization, existence checks, ambiguity handling, or localized aliases for user-supplied ledger identifiers and feature names.
items.title: User command placeholders lack an input-validation contract

segments.summary: Reviewed all 189 core lines and the complete assigned document source unit. The workflow has strong authority boundaries, provenance, closure-state, and semantic-completion rules; material adversarial gaps remain around transactional projection writes, GUI split criteria, deterministic compile and seal gates, failed-batch recovery, registry security/concurrency/lifecycle, subject-ref selection, validator failure semantics, scaling thresholds, and command input validation.

Where are the numeric compile-sharding thresholds and subagent result-acceptance rules owned?
